title: Life-cycle rules, versioning, Object Lock and retention

videos.script: Lesson 1 ended with an overwrite that could not be undone. This lesson is about three ways to stop that, and what each one costs. {{undo}} The first is versioning. A bucket that keeps versions never loses a write, and a delete only hides the file behind a marker. You delete one, and bring it back. {{versions}} Keeping everything has a price. A table rewritten every night is a new full copy every night, and a short program shows a year of that adding up. {{bill}} The second is a life-cycle rule, which moves old files to cheaper classes and deletes what nobody needs. moto stores the rule and never runs it, and you will see that plainly. {{rules}} The third is Object Lock. A locked version cannot be deleted before its date, not even by the account that owns it. {{lock}} moto refuses the delete, and then lets you take the lock off. S3 would never allow that, and the lesson shows exactly where the imitation gives way. {{weak}}
